📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Industry observers note that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds revealed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

According to recent reports, today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

According to recent reports, at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

But in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an problem Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

According to recent reports, others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

Industry observers note that the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Recent findings suggest that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

In a recent development, the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been confirmed, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The fresh trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the latest production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently said she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • It has been revealed that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

It has been revealed that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

Sources indicate that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical strategy to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s newly introduced head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

In a recent development, maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

It has been revealed that was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a massive team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

In a recent development, there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

In a recent development, phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

In a recent development, patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

According to recent reports, “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

In a recent development, even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

In a recent development, the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the initiative of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

It has been revealed that [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

In a recent development, changed the proposal for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

We always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

It just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

Industry observers note that he was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

Industry observers note that every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Industry observers note that haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that reveals personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We had to change the proposal a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

But if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the big goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

Recent findings suggest that haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

Recent findings suggest that to most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very vital in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

It has been revealed that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 16:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:30 EST, 19 November 2026.

Andriy Shevchenko has accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of trying to persuade the Ukrainian FA to find someone to falsely take the blame for the winger's failed drugs test.

Mudryk, now on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea, was suspended for 20 months between November 2024 and July 2026 after testing positive for banned substance meldonium in October 2024.

In an interview, Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian FA (UAF), claiming the substance entered his body while on international duty.

'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine,' he stated.

But Shevchenko, president of the UAF, described the accusations as 'baseless slander'. Shevchenko added: 'His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample,' he told Tribuna. 'Such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.'.

In a recent development, shevchenko stated investigations had failed to establish how the substance entered Mudryk's system. He added that national team staff complied with Chelsea's request not to give Mudryk medication, and that two of his personal specialists were allowed at training camps.

Mykhailo Mudryk (left) has been accused of 'baseless slander' by Ukraine FA (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko after he blamed his failed drugs test on the national team's setup.

'If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it,' Shevchenko remarked, demanding a public retraction and apology otherwise.

Mudryk's representatives have been approached for comment.

The 25-year-old was initially handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

In a bombshell two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel, Mudryk laid the blame for his situation with the Ukraine national team - something Shevchenko vehemently denies.

According to recent reports, 'Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally,' the UAF president, who also played for Chelsea during his time, remarked in a statement to The Athletic.

'After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps,' he continued.

'The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine but is yet to represent them since his ban was overturned.

Sources indicate that 'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

'I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.'.

In his interview, Mudryk - who is yet to add to his 28 caps for his country since returning from his ban - laid the blame at Ukraine's door.

According to recent reports, 'I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It's a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,' the winger said.

It has been revealed that 'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

Sources indicate that 'I was at home and Chelsea's management came to see me and they remarked we needed to talk. Then they say you've returned a positive doping test and now you're facing a ban.

'You can't believe it's true. You can't believe this is happening to you. If I'd ever taken anything anywhere, I'd have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

He is presently on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea but has only played once so far this season.

According to recent reports, 'At least I'd have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that's the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

'Otherwise there'd be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don't hear them.

'At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you're falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You're flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don't wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.'.

Mudryk, who joined Chelsea for £89million from Shakhtar Donetsk, has only made one substitute appearance for Tottenham so far this season due to an ankle injury.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 20:04.

Florian Wirtz produced a stellar performance as Liverpool registered an emphatic 4-0 victory over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring for the Reds after Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, before Wirtz doubled their advantage in the first half.

Liverpool dominated possession after the interval and added two more goals, with Rio Ngumoha making history for the Reds and Victor Munoz also getting on the scoresheet.

While the Reds remain third in the Premier League table, they have closed the gap on second-placed Manchester City to one point and are seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola is now unbeaten in his seven Premier League matches against the Red Devils, with only legendary Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp boasting a longer record, having gone eight games without defeat against the same opposition.

The German international came under heavy criticism from Jamie Carragher at the start of the season as he struggled to make an impact.

Wirtz has gradually rediscovered his confidence and delivered a top-class performance against the Red Devils, creating as many as 10 chances.

According to Opta Joe, Wirtz's tally was the highest by any player in a Premier League match since David Silva created 11 chances against West Bromwich Albion in March 2015.

Wirtz has now registered three goals and five assists across all competitions for the Reds this season, and those numbers are expected to rise in the coming months.

While the victory over a struggling Man Utd side reduced to 10 men may not provide a complete picture, there are signs that Liverpool's players are gradually getting to grips with Iraola's demands.

There was greater cohesion and better team chemistry throughout the contest, and the side could become even stronger once Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley return from injury.

Wirtz has covered considerable ground in every match, and his work rate has been second to none, but the end product had been missing.

Iraola will hope that Wirtz can build on this performance and help Liverpool reach new heights as the season progresses.

Industry News: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

In a recent development, “Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

In a recent development, “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, remarked. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

Recent findings suggest that the home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

Recent findings suggest that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous latest West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a massive evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Industry observers note that major? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

In a recent development, jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Recent findings suggest that leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

According to recent reports, A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

According to recent reports, “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

Sources indicate that [It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have mentioned it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

In a recent development, it’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

It has been revealed that exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

In a recent development, energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

Recent findings suggest that we have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

Sources indicate that [Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

Recent findings suggest that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

Industry observers note that anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as rapidly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

Industry observers note that but Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

In a recent development, jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

Recent findings suggest that there are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

Recent findings suggest that this is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the fresh boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Industry observers note that mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always crucial to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s notable not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Industry observers note that good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

Sources indicate that the architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat noted. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a substantial relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a massive win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

In a recent development, "I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

According to recent reports, growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

It has been revealed that "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat stated. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

"I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat said. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a massive change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

Industry observers note that as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat remarked.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she said. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

According to recent reports, that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

Industry observers note that "The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she mentioned.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Latest South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
  • Australian sport was still in shock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Latest South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

Australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between New South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

The impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

Hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

It has been revealed that that February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

According to recent reports, it was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

Industry observers note that that grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

There was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is remarked that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

Owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

It has been revealed that owono has become a pariah. It is mentioned that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, stated the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

Recent findings suggest that no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

Some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. It has been reported that his brother, who is also a footballer, has been the victim of abuse because of his association with Owono.

Owono has only communicated through a statement released by his club. 'These are the most difficult days of my life,' he wrote. 'I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.'.

Sources indicate that I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. He lost his daughter, Danika, to cancer when she was just 33, in 2019. And in 1982, three years before he won the world featherweight title at Loftus Road, he nearly quit boxing altogether.

According to recent reports, in the 12th fight of his professional career, McGuigan fought a Nigerian boxer called Young Ali at the World Sporting Club in Mayfair. He still remembers the clink of cutlery coming from the diners who were sitting ringside that night. That sound still takes him back.

It has been revealed that mcGuigan still remembers the sequence of punches that put Young Ali down in the sixth round of the fight. He saw his opponent's eyes roll back in his head and a feeling of dread washed over him. Young Ali, just 21, fell into a coma from which he never emerged and died five months later.

I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan (right) about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies.

'There was the horror of that and we sat and we waited and we prayed that he would be better and he never got better,' McGuigan told me. 'I didn't know whether I wanted to continue boxing. I thought: "If I can do this to somebody…"'.

In a recent development, he shuddered when he talked about Owono. 'Other tragedies happen and other terrible things happen,' he said. 'Life is a struggle. Something like that, you never leave it behind you.

Industry observers note that 'It is something invisible and it depends how emotionally vulnerable he is. He may never be the same again but I hope he is able to overcome it.'.

It has been revealed that there are others out there in sport, still trying to overcome it. Think of Matt Petgrave, the Sheffield Steelers ice-hockey player who was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after his skate fatally cut the neck of Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson in an Elite Ice Hockey League match at Sheffield Arena in October 2023.

In a recent development, think of Jochen Mass, the Formula One driver, who spent years blaming himself for the death of Gilles Villeneuve during qualifying for the Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder in 1982, because he slowed and moved to the right in front of Villeneuve. The Ferrari ran into the back of Mass and flipped in grotesque cartwheels across the track.

Think of Matthias Behr, the German fencer who killed his opponent, Vladimir Smirnov, at the 1982 World Fencing Championships in Rome when Behr's foil blade broke during a match, penetrated the Ukrainian fencer's mask and pierced his eye.

Think of Gary Cully, the Irish fighter, who learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves, had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

'What a character and a gent,' Cully wrote in tribute to Reeves. 'It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother.'.

Nottingham Panthers' Adam Johnson died in October 2023 when opponent Matt Petgrave's skate cut his neck during a match.

Gary Cully (left), the Irish fighter, learned this week that his last opponent, Lee Reeves (right), had died after spending three months in a coma following their bout in Dublin in August.

Dr Victor Thompson, a prominent UK clinical sports psychologist, has studied the effect on competitors of being involved in the death of a rival.

Recent findings suggest that 'The biggest thing a player will have had to absorb normally is bad performance,' Dr Thompson claims. 'Now he has to absorb the fact that he was involved in somebody dying. He will be trying to work out was it his fault? Is he to blame? And all of that, because the emotions are so high, gets associated with playing the sport in question.

'So when Sean Abbott thought about going out there again, when he thought about putting his pads on, or putting his kit on and being around team-mates or the smell of the cricket bat – it'll all be associated to that very traumatic day.'.

University of North Carolina academic John M Silva III argued that aggression in sport is defined in two categories: hostile aggression and instrumental aggression. Hostile is when the main aim is to cause harm or injury to your opponent. Instrumental is aggression for a purpose, perhaps ball recovery or to sow doubt in an opponent’s mind.

The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy. Whether forgiveness is extended to or opprobrium visited on the competitor who has caused the death of another.

Industry observers note that that interpretation was used against Petgrave, who was notorious for having a bad disciplinary record on the ice. Some likened the action which fatally injured Johnson to a kung-fu kick and drew a link between it and some of his past behaviour. He was mercilessly trolled on social media. Team-mates, and many ice hockey fans, leapt to his defence and mentioned any suggestion his action was deliberate was fanciful. They said his unusual action in lifting his left skate high was a direct result of being knocked off balance by a collision.

Petgrave could not return to ice hockey immediately even if he had wanted to. It was a full 18 months before the Crown Prosecution Service and South Yorkshire Police decided there was no realistic prospect of conviction for manslaughter and that no criminal charges should be brought against the 34-year-old Canadian.

In the intervening period, Petgrave's family set up a crowdfunding page, pointing out that he was unable to work or to return home until the CPS had decided whether to press charges. The page raised nearly £20,000 from well-wishers.

The interpretation of a player's actions at a time of high stress, frustration or adversarial combat is often central to the reaction to a sporting tragedy - as it was for Petgrave.

Petgrave did receive widespread support from inside his sport, with a standing ovation at his Sheffield side's next home match, while he was beginning 18 months under investigation.

According to recent reports, 'This has been the most painful and overwhelming period of our lives,' a message from Petgrave's family mentioned at the bottom of the page. 'Watching someone I love go through this has been incredibly difficult.

'Despite everything, we are doing our best to stay strong, and the support and kindness from so many people have been a source of strength. We continue to recognise the heartbreaking nature of this situation, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected. We hold on to hope that this will soon come to an end.'.

It has been revealed that petgrave now plies his trade in the minor league ECHL for the Indy Fuel, a team based in Fishers, Indiana. He is an ever-present this season, playing opponents like the Wheeling Nailers, the Greenville Swamp Rabbits, the Kalamazoo Wings and the Bloomington Bison.

In a recent development, 'We understand the responsibility that comes with the great support we receive from this community,' Sean Hallett, CEO of Hallett Sports, which owns the Fuel, said when they hired Petgrave. 'We are confident he will be a positive addition to our team and our city.'.

Sources indicate that I wrote to the Fuel, asking if there was any chance of speaking to Petgrave. They did not respond. The reticence is understandable and, in many ways, laudable. Players involved in this kind of tragedy are preoccupied with respect for the victims' families and the sensitivities that come with such terrible grief. There is nothing they can say or do to make it better.

Sometimes, it is the other way round. Sometimes, it is the family of a lost loved one who find a way to ease the pain of a sportsman eaten up by shame for inadvertently causing the death of a competitor.

It has been revealed that mass, who died last year, blamed himself for the sickening crash that killed the most exciting, charismatic, talented, electrifying driver in Formula One. As Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track until he came to rest in the catch-fencing by the side of the circuit. He died of catastrophic injuries later that evening, aged 32.

According to recent reports, mass was absolved of responsibility. It was a tragic accident. Villeneuve was running hot after a disagreement with his team-mate Didier Pironi and was pushing even his own boundaries. There were any number of extenuating circumstances but Mass still blamed himself. He retired from the sport the same season.

As Gilles Villeneuve's Ferrari cartwheeled across the track, breaking into pieces, he was flung clear of the wreckage still strapped to his seat, catapulting across the track.

Despite being absolved of responsibility, Jochen Mass (pictured in 2019) blamed himself for the accident and retired from the sport the same year.

In a recent development, it was years later when he felt a tap on the shoulder as he was sitting on a plane. He looked up to see Villeneuve's son, Jacques, the 1997 F1 world champion, standing over him.

In a recent development, 'I felt so guilty about what had happened and then suddenly, there was Jacques,' Mass recalled. 'He mentioned: "Jochen, our family – we never blamed you. It was a racing incident – just a wrong decision by the two of you."'.

All the shame that Mass felt ebbed away. He found his own peace just as Behr found redemption by sheltering the grandchildren of Smirnov and his widow, Emma, at his home in Germany to protect them from the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Sources indicate that behr, tortured by guilt about the accident that killed Smirnov, had written to Emma 30 years ago but the letter was lost. When he did not receive a reply, he was convinced that Smirnov's widow blamed him for killing her husband.

In a recent development, they finally met when a television documentary crew brought them together and Emma reassured Behr that she had never held him responsible. Behr has suffered from depression and suicidal thoughts because of flashbacks to the fatal accident.

'They are always there,' Behr noted later. 'Even if I go into a liquor store and see vodka with the Smirnoff label on it, the thoughts of what happened immediately come back to me. But now that I am playing a part in the lives of Vladimir's grandchildren, it has come full circle for me. It was a gift for me. I can finally give something back.'.

Sources indicate that maybe Abbott has been trying to give something back all these years, too. Perhaps the fine career he has had is his tribute to Hughes. He has represented Australia in one-day and Twenty20 cricket and is the all-time leading wicket-taker in the Substantial Bash League. He has represented Surrey in English cricket and was part of Australia's World Cup winning squad in 2023.

Industry observers note that many had worried that Abbott would not play again after Hughes' death. Not your fault, young man. Easy to say, harder to grasp amid the grief and the disbelief. But there was an outpouring of support for him, including from Hughes' family.

Perhaps the fine career 2023 World Cup winner Sean Abbott (bottom right) has had is his tribute to Hughes.

Recent findings suggest that that afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I asked him about the day's play as he came off. He mentioned he was happy with how it had gone. Afterwards, I sat in the stand with Abbott's team-mate Nathan Lyon, the Australia spinner, who spoke movingly about Hughes and about Abbott. At the end of the interview I thanked him for making the time to speak to me in such difficult circumstances. 'Too easy, mate,' he said.

Except it wasn't too easy. Inside, Lyon and the rest of Australian cricket were still in agony. Later that day, Lyon complained to Cricket Australia that he had not been expecting to be asked about Hughes. He was upset about my questions. I had made a misjudgment. Things were still too raw.

In a recent development, lyon was comfortable talking about Abbott, though. 'The way Sean has carried himself through the whole incident, well, credit goes to him,' Lyon mentioned. 'He is a very impressive bloke. I've got a lot of time for him. He will do anything to help anyone out. He always puts mates first. He always has your back. He is a typical good mate. I'm proud to call him a mate.

'I think (Abbott not playing again) went through the minds of a few of us. But natural instinct will come over and you do what you do best and if that's play cricket, you go out and play cricket. It's about being around your mates and the mates who are there with him now, they're the guys who are going to get him through it.'.

In a recent development, abbott has never spoken about the tragedy. He gave written evidence in January 2016 to the inquest into Hughes' death.

Recent findings suggest that 'I saw him start to sway and I ran to the other end of the pitch and I held the right side of his head with my left hand,' Abbott wrote. 'I remained on the field until Phillip was placed on the medicab and then returned to the changing room. Once in the changing room I felt confused and upset, I had a headache, people kept coming up to me but I cannot recall what they said.'.

Much of the inquest was dominated by suggestions that Hughes had been subjected to a barrage of short balls and sledging. The inquest heard that Abbott's bowling partner, Doug Bollinger, had said to Hughes 'I'm going to kill you' at one stage during the game. Bollinger denied that accusation. Abbott was exonerated of any responsibility for the tragedy that unfolded.

Only rarely are there glimpses of the impact that Hughes' death has had on him. At a tribute to Hughes on the tenth anniversary of his death, Abbott broke down and wept at the end of the minute's silence at the SCG. One of his team-mates put an arm around his shoulders to try to comfort him.

Abbott at Hughes' funeral in his hometown of Macksville, Australia, in 2014.

According to recent reports, paris Saint-Germain are reportedly one of six leading European clubs interested in Brighton and Hove Albion left-back Maxim De Cuyper, according to journalist Ekrem Konur. The Belgium international has played regularly in the Premier League since the start of 2026-27 and is under contract with the Seagulls until June 2030.

With attackers Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue both injured, PSG must decide quickly whether to make do with their current squad or use the winter transfer window to act.

In January, another area of the pitch could be strengthened by the French capital club: left-back. Lucas Digne has been limited to little playing time, and the double Champions League holders are considering a upcoming left-back as back-up or alternative to Nuno Mendes, at least to give the Portugal international a rest from time to time.

With that in mind, the Paris hierarchy has shown interest in a Premier League left-back: Maxim De Cuyper. According to information relayed by Konur, PSG are part of a list of six renowned European clubs following the situation of the Belgian defender.

Sources indicate that his significant playing time in England this season is one of the reasons he has attracted attention. Two Premier League giants - Arsenal and Liverpool - are also quoted as interested such as Juventus, AC Milan and AS Roma.

According to recent reports, there is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. In a recent development, at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Industry observers note that dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second revealed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

According to recent reports, max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

Industry observers note that as Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a fresh contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, “A joy to have him,” mentioned Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

In a recent development, dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” mentioned Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Industry observers note that dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. Industry observers note that it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. Sources indicate that arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

According to recent reports, given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies remarked Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

In a recent development, the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

Sources indicate that for much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

Sources indicate that when asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil mentioned: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”.

Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

Sources indicate that this season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#129085. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
